findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search_vacation_rentals" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search 70,000+ independently-owned vacation rentals in 86 countries, and find every way to book each one — including the host's own direct booking site, which O…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "search_vacation_rentals" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: Search 70,000+ independently-owned vacation rentals in 86 countries, and find every way to book each one — including the host's own direct booking site, which O…

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "search_vacation_rentals" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: Search 70,000+ independently-owned vacation rentals in 86 countries, and find every way to book each one — including the host's own direct booking site, which O…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_listing_details, find_direct_booking · Private data: refine_search, find_direct_booking · Public sink: refine_search.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_listing_details, find_direct_booking · Private data: refine_search, find_direct_booking · Public sink: refine_search

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
